record_body:
Account summary
- Enterprise financial services. Building internal + customer-facing GenAI assistants (call summarization + KB search + policy Q&A).
- Strong preference for Dedicated reserved GPU pools in VPC due to regulatory posture and noisy-neighbor concerns.
- Primary gap: safe staged rollouts for Dedicated pools. They have been burned by “all-at-once” model/runtime/config updates causing queue depth spikes and p95 latency breaches.

Firmographics / environment notes
- HQ: NA (US). Internal requirement to keep inference traffic in US regions.
- Deployment: Dedicated reserved pools (VPC). Discussed Private as future option for a subset of workloads.
- Identity: SSO/SAML required for Console access. Need scoped roles for approve/abort.
- Audit: Must provide an auditable trail for: rollout create/update, stage approvals, aborts, auto-holds/rollbacks, and policy changes. Export to Splunk/SIEM expected.

Current workload + requirements (as captured from eval calls)
- Workload types:
  - Chat-style assistant (employee-facing) with peak concurrency during business hours.
  - Doc-search / RAG (embeddings + rerank) for policy and product documentation.
  - Summarization of customer calls (batch + near-real-time).
- Performance targets (stated as “guardrails,” not contract yet):
  - p95 end-to-end latency for chat: <= 1.5s under normal load; wants clear behavior under saturation (graceful degradation).
  - Error budget: wants alerting when 5xx/timeouts rise during rollouts.
  - Queue depth is a key signal they watch; they want “stop-the-line” when it grows.
- Rollout governance requirements:
  - Staged rollout: multi-stage (e.g., 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with explicit evaluation windows.
  - Gates: p95 latency, 5xx rate, timeout rate, GPU utilization, queue depth.
  - Missing/late metrics must fail safe (hold) vs advance.
  - Manual approval required between stages for initial rollout period (at least through 2026H1).

Beta participation notes
- They agreed in principle to be a beta customer for Dedicated staged rollouts, contingent on:
  - Clear rollback/abort semantics.
  - Audit log event schema review by their SecOps + GRC.
  - “No surprise” traffic shifts: deterministic allocation and ability to preview the plan.
- Internal quote (security review): “If we can’t prove who approved a change and when, we can’t ship it.”
- Internal quote (platform lead): “A bad rollout can saturate a reserved pool and we have no escape hatch today.”

Key activity timeline (recent)
- 2025-12-03: Evaluation kickoff; reviewed Dedicated pool sizing + historical saturation issues.
- 2026-01-09: Security review: audit logging + retention + RBAC expectations. Requested example events and export fields.
- 2026-01-22: Beta kickoff call (Fireflies meeting_9f3c2a1b). Walked through staged rollouts concept, gates, manual approvals, and what Redwood will support in beta.
- 2026-02-21: Follow-up thread confirming they want stage approvals restricted to a small group; asked about “auto-hold vs auto-rollback” policy and evaluator failure modes.

Stakeholders (customer-side, partial)
- Platform Engineering (owner of Dedicated pool operations)
- SecOps/GRC (audit logging + change management)
- App team (assistant product)

Redwood internal team touches
- Rachel Kim (owner / enterprise coordination)
- Emily Zhao (SE / VPC + connectivity)
- Marcus Lin + Kevin Osei looped for audit log schema + export pipeline expectations
- Lauren Bishop looped for Dedicated requirements alignment

Open questions
- Do they need per-route staged rollouts within a pool or is pool-level acceptable for v1? (they said pool-level is acceptable if routing guarantees deterministic splits by tenant/app route)
- Audit log retention expectations: they mentioned 1 year searchable, 7 years archive (needs confirmation).
- Whether they require quality gating initially (they said “nice to have”; focus is reliability signals first).

Notes / risks
- They will likely not progress to procurement without a committed beta timeline and written spec for approvals + audit events.
- They specifically called out needing an escalation path during rollouts (who to page, who can approve/abort under incident).

Links / artifacts referenced
- Fireflies: meeting_9f3c2a1b (beta kickoff), meeting_3d0a77e4 (security review)
- Gmail threads: lauren_bishop/thread_91aa03fd, marcus_lin/thread_2a9c8d73, rachel_kim/thread_0d9b1b6c
- Support: SUP-3981 (audit trail request), SUP-3924 (traffic split confusion)

Next steps (internal)
- Provide them a one-pager: Dedicated staged rollouts beta scope + limitations + gating defaults.
- Confirm allowlist + feature flag plan for their tenant, plus required pool headroom policy during partial rollout stages.
- Schedule audit log schema walkthrough with Marcus Lin/Kevin Osei + their SecOps; capture required fields for Splunk mapping.
